# Key findings - Riverbend University workforce, as at 31 December 2025

*Generated by `run_pipeline.py`. All data is synthetic.*

**Workforce size.** 3,205 staff (2,879 FTE), up from 3,107 at the end of 2021.

**Turnover.** Total separation rate for non-casual staff was 13.4% in 2025 (16.4% in 2022); the resignation rate was 8.2%.

**Who resigns.** Resignation is associated with employment type (chi-square = 67.9, df = 1, p < 0.001, Cramer's V = 0.08 - a real but small effect). Holding other factors constant, fixed-term staff have 1.68x the odds of resigning, staff with under two years' service 1.38x, and Digital & Technology staff 1.70x. Gender and staff group are not significant at the 5% level.

**Digital & Technology.** Pooled 2022-2025 resignation rate of 11.6% against 7.3% elsewhere: a difference of 4.4 percentage points (95% CI 2.2 to 6.5).

**Gender.** Women are 57% of staff but 34% of senior staff (Level D/E and HEW 10+). The overall gender pay gap is 12.4%; comparing like with like (same classification) it is 1.3%. Around 90% of the gap is therefore structural - who holds senior roles - rather than unequal pay at the same level.

**Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander representation.** 1.6% of headcount (95% CI 1.2% to 2.1%) against a 3% target; 6.5% of staff have not disclosed. At the current hiring mix (2.5% of hires) representation does not reach the target within 10 years; at 5% of hires it reaches the target in about 4 years; at 8% it reaches the target in about 2 years.

**Retirement exposure.** 14% of ongoing staff in the Faculty of Engineering (39 people) reach 65 within five years, against 7% university-wide.
